solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Information to pass to defender?

parts.note: to pass the ball to a teammate is to feed it to them
a back is a defending player in football or rugby

explanation.surface: A coach wonders what message to give the player guarding the goal.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the football picture: FEED is to pass the ball, a BACK is a defender.
explanation.definitionFit: Feedback is information given in response about how something went.

clue.text: Plain girl set up to enter item in sports programme

indicators.note: to enter means these letters go inside the other piece

parts.note: an event is one contest on a sports programme

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the word is read upwards, i.e. backwards

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, short for Diana

explanation.surface: A modest young woman is entered in a race at an athletics meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'set up' means read upwards, giving ID; 'Plain' is the adjective obvious, not a plain-looking girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain as an adjective means obvious or clear to see, a synonym for evident.

clue.text: Italian poet's output ultimately digested by Scandinavian

indicators.note: something digested is taken inside, so this letter goes within the other word

parts.note: a Dane is a person from Denmark, a Scandinavian country

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word output

explanation.surface: A poet's work is lapped up by a Nordic reader.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after poet stands for 'is', linking definition to wordplay: T, the last letter of output, goes inside DANE.
explanation.definitionFit: Dante Alighieri was the Florentine author of the Divine Comedy.

clue.text: Reportedly everything a leather worker needs?

indicators.note: reportedly means the word is said aloud and the answer matches its sound

parts.note: all means everything

explanation.surface: Rumour has it a leatherworker requires every tool going.
explanation.definitionFit: An awl is a pointed tool for piercing holes in leather, a basic need for a saddler or cobbler.

clue.text: Unexpected win associated with a monk's blood relation

indicators.note: something unexpected is out of the usual order, signalling these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A surprise victory is linked to a cousin of some monk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unexpected' rearranges WIN, A and MONKS; 'associated with' merely joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: A kinswoman is a female relative by birth.

clue.text: Girl needing hot bath finally after game

indicators.note: after places the following letters behind the game abbreviation

parts.note: RU is rugby union, a game

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of each of the words hot and bath

explanation.surface: A girl wants a hot soak after playing sport.
explanation.walkthrough: RU (rugby union) comes first, 'after' putting T and H, the final letters of 'hot bath', behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruth is a female given name, as of the Old Testament heroine.

clue.text: Rhode Island's one and only minced meat dish

parts.note: RI is the postal abbreviation for Rhode Island, with the possessive S
sole means one and only

explanation.surface: A state boasts its unique speciality of ground meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A rissole is a fried cake of chopped meat coated in breadcrumbs.

clue.text: It isn't commonly a stain or blemish

parts.note: 'T is a contracted form of it, as in 'tis
ain't is the colloquial, nonstandard form of isn't

explanation.surface: Someone insists, in casual speech, that a mark is not a stain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Commonly' marks informal speech: 'T AIN'T is a folksy way of saying 'it isn't'.
explanation.definitionFit: A taint is a trace of contamination or a moral flaw, much like a blot.

clue.text: Lowly-sounding bearing

indicators.note: sounding means we hear the word aloud and take its homophone

parts.note: mean can mean lowly or humble, as in of mean birth

explanation.surface: Someone carries themselves in a way that seems humble.
explanation.definitionFit: Mien is a person's look or manner, their demeanour or carriage.

clue.text: Touch down by mistake in fallen earth and rock

parts.note: to land is to touch down, as an aircraft does
a slip is a small mistake

explanation.surface: A pilot accidentally comes down in a pile of rubble.
explanation.definitionFit: A landslip is a mass of soil and stone sliding down a slope, a landslide.

clue.text: Passion not many displayed for European plant

parts.note: fever is intense excitement or passion
few means not many

explanation.surface: Hardly anyone showed enthusiasm for a continental flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Feverfew is an aromatic daisy-like herb native to Europe, once used against fevers.

clue.text: Songbird destroying leaf, if red

indicators.note: destroying breaks the words apart so their letters can be rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bird is ravaging a scarlet leaf.
explanation.definitionFit: The fieldfare is a large thrush that winters in Britain, a type of songbird.

clue.text: It may be sworn round at hotel

parts.note: O is round in shape
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone curses loudly while drinking a round in a hotel bar.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as cursing, but an oath is sworn in the sense of a solemn promise.
explanation.definitionFit: One swears an oath, the vow taken in court or on taking office.

clue.text: Southern gallery accommodating high-class sculpture

indicators.note: accommodating means holding something inside, so the letter goes within the gallery

parts.note: the Tate is the famous London art gallery
U is the old British label for upper-class usage

explanation.surface: A gallery in the south finds room for a smart piece of sculpture.
explanation.walkthrough: U meaning upper-class comes from Nancy Mitford's 'U and non-U' distinction in British speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A statue is a carved or cast figure, one kind of sculpture.

clue.text: Pester chaps involved in civil wrong

indicators.note: involved in means these letters are wrapped within the other word

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law
men means chaps

explanation.surface: Fellows mixed up in a lawsuit harass someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To torment is to harass or annoy persistently, as to pester does.

clue.text: Greek character, priest, consuming small cereal

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: consuming means taking in, so the letter is eaten up inside the priest

parts.note: Eli is the priest in the Old Testament who raised Samuel
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A Greek priest is eating a small breakfast bowl.
explanation.definitionFit: Muesli is a breakfast mix of oats, nuts and dried fruit, a cereal.

clue.text: Note about one oddly like a big cat

indicators.note: about means placed around, so the note goes round the jumbled letters

parts.note: a line is a short note, as in drop me a line

indicators.note: oddly suggests the word one is behaving strangely and is rearranged

explanation.surface: A memo about someone strangely resembling a lion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' here means around, not concerning; 'oddly' scrambles one into EON.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonine means lion-like, the lion being a big cat.

clue.text: Muslim ruler old poem recalled

indicators.note: recalled is read as called back, so the poem is taken in the reverse direction

parts.note: rime is an old spelling of rhyme, a poem, as in The Rime of the Ancient Mariner

explanation.surface: A sultan remembers verses from long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: An emir is a prince or commander in Islamic countries.

clue.text: Second outsize European deer

parts.note: a mo is a moment or second, as in wait a mo
OS is the abbreviation for outsize on clothing

explanation.surface: A huge continental stag comes in second place.
explanation.definitionFit: The moose is the largest species of deer, called elk in Europe.

clue.text: College lecturer breaking into a gift

parts.note: a don is a university college teacher, especially at Oxford or Cambridge

indicators.note: breaking shatters the words so their letters re-form in a new order

explanation.surface: An academic bursts into someone's house bearing a present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking into' looks like an insertion signal, but only 'breaking' works, scrambling 'into a' to ATION.
explanation.definitionFit: A donation is something given freely, especially to charity.

clue.text: Fortress you and I observed in rocky peak

indicators.note: observed in means seen inside, so these letters sit within the peak

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, especially on Dartmoor
we means you and I

explanation.surface: We were spotted on a craggy summit.
explanation.walkthrough: A tor is a rocky outcrop on a hilltop, typical of Dartmoor in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A tower can be a fortified building or stronghold, like the Tower of London.

clue.text: Prediction supporting English players

parts.note: for means in favour of, supporting
the cast are the players in a production

explanation.surface: A forecast of how the national team will do.
explanation.definitionFit: A forecast is a prediction, as of the weather.

clue.text: First vessel to be capsized

indicators.note: a capsized boat is upside down, so in a down clue the word is turned over

parts.note: a pot is a vessel for holding things

explanation.surface: The leading boat is going to overturn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' suggests a ship to go with 'capsized', but it is a pot.
explanation.definitionFit: Top as an adjective means highest-ranked or first, as in top prize.

clue.text: Husband in peruke, a politician once

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the letter goes within the wig

parts.note: a peruke is an old-fashioned wig

explanation.surface: An old-time statesman wears a powdered wig.
explanation.definitionFit: The Whigs were a British party of the 17th to 19th centuries, forerunners of the Liberals.

clue.text: Ambassador attending qualifying round

parts.note: HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador
at means present at, attending

explanation.surface: A diplomat turns up at a preliminary contest.
explanation.definitionFit: A heat is a preliminary race whose winners go through to the final.

clue.text: Former railway employee, an international trader

parts.note: ex means former
a porter carries luggage at a railway station

explanation.surface: A one-time station worker now deals in overseas goods.
explanation.definitionFit: An exporter sells goods abroad, trading across borders.
